I wanted a portable TV that I could walk around the house with, sit outside, or be at a park/beach and watch - after all it's supposed to be portable, right? Well, unless you have a 1000 feet antenna cable, this is not a portable TV. I live in a major metropolitan city where we have many TV stations, and with the telescoping antenna the TV comes with, I can barely pick up 2 stations - which were unwatchable as they constantly froze. When I connected it to my houses's rooftop antenna, the TV picked up an amazing 30 channels and the picture quality was excellent - very nice fluid motion. The sound is OK for the size of the speakers, don't expect a THX-certified system - it is what it is. It comes with a built-in flip-out stand which you can place on a nightstand, floor, etc. and an attachable stand that you can use for a more permanent location such as a kitchen counter. FYI, the setup process is pretty much straightforward and you don't really need the instructions - which were wrong with respect to the use of the remote control; I guess they must've changed the remote, but did not change the instructions. For such an inexpensive TV, it comes with a number of features you wouldn't expect, such as a Sleep Timer, Daylight Savings Time selection, 5 adjustments for the picture quality, etc. - very nice and unexpected. I haven't checked the battery life yet, but from what I've read in other reviews, it doesn't seem to last for a long time. I'd recommend shopping around for a spare battery so that you can have it charged and ready to go if you're at a park or beach. I definitely recommend purchasing a better portable antenna as the included antenna is pretty much worthless. All in all, I do recommend the TV as the picture quality at this price can't be beat.

First, it's important to acknowledge that the Iconia A200 is absolutely unusable without a screen protector; within a few minutes using the device without a screen protector, my fingerprints were everywhere on the screen, creating a huge visual distraction. But if you've used any touchscreen device, you probably already know this.I spent nearly an hour with the Fosmon screen protectors, and I'm glad I bought a five-pack because otherwise I never would have been certain that it's the product itself that's frustrating and not just my efforts.The problem (as mentioned in other reviews for the 1- and 3-pack) is that these appear to be cut with extraordinary precision, so there is absolutely zero room for any type of mistake. And you must get it right the first time, because if you lift & reposition the screen protector, you WILL pick up some dust particulate which will be very obvious once you've finished applying the screen protector.I've just finished applying the FOURTH of the five screen protectors, and I've decided that this is the best result I'm going to get: only one visible dust particle embedded in a spot just outside the viewable screen, plus several spots that just can't be scraped away.  I had to throw away the first two screen protectors because I ended up positioning the screen protector upside-down (there's a tiny circle cut out for the camera, and if you install the product as instructed, it will only work if the device is facing AWAY from you), and an added problem is that the circle isn't actually punched out, so when you position the screen protector, the little circle slides under the screen protector, requiring that you lift it to remove the little circle.I worried that the tremendous pressure required with the cardboard applicator to remove air bubbles might actually damage the tablet's screen or its internals, but so far there's no sign of damage.Each time I tried to install the product, there was always one edge that was "off" -- visually I couldn't see it, no matter how close I looked, but the air pockets wouldn't dissipate because the edge was just over the lip/edge.  I repositioned carefully several times, until eventually there were too many dust particles embedded, and I had to throw away another screen protector.I finally surrendered: there will always be one edge that isn't quite right, so there will be air bubbles.If you do buy this product, don't follow the instructions! Instead, start your positioning efforts on the "tiny circle" for the camera -- make sure you remove the entire circle (both masks plus the screen protector itself) before you start applying it onto the tablet, and carefully position the circle centered perfectly (perfectly, perfectly, perfectly) over the camera hole and with the top edge aligned perfectly (perfectly, perfectly, perfectly) with the top edge of the device.  Remember that unless you have a semiconductor-quality "clean room," you'll only get ONE chance to apply the screen protector without dust particles getting embedded (be practical, as I was, and just buy a multi-pack, knowing that you'll end up using several "to learn with."I honestly don't know if other screen-protector products are better or worse for this device, but I wish the instructions had been much more detailed, had mentioned the need to position over the camera, and had warned that a minimum of 10-15 minutes would be required to install the screen protector (if everything goes well).

A rather loud part of the song welcomed these terribly bright blue LED lights on the front of the amplifier, and I at once said "no.".Since Beautiful Day is a pop-ish song, I decided to play Pink Floyd's On the Turning Away (A Momentary Lapse of Reason) with it's climbing, smooth, resonating, bassy beginning and crisp overall sound. It sounded acceptable, far better than any $50 ipod speaker dock, but no cigar. I know that sometimes a lack of output power can lead to lacking performance (learned that with the Fisher), so I turned up the volume on both my phone and the Pyle to about 60%. This is where the horrid distortion began, most notable in vocals. Putting my ear close to the speaker, I concluded that the distortion was coming out of the Tweeter (the part of the speaker that is used for the med-high pitched sounds (ex. guitar, cymbals of drums, female voices)). This was definitely a no-no, seeing as its the exact reason I opted for a more powerful amp.-----GOOD-----+small+better than the 15w+reasonably priced+good looking when the horrid blue lights are off-----BAD------bigger than the 15w-still not good enough-I wouldn't pay more than $20 for it, since it is so disappointing-BLUE LIGHTS - These lights are as obnoxious as Justin Bieber's fans. No, really, I'm serious.Just don't buy it. I simply can't recommend any more Pyle products after putting $100 into 2 of their products only to return both. Unless you listen in complete silence, have speakers laying around, don't care about sound quality, don't mind blinding (and even worse: unpredictable) LED lights shining in your eyes, AND have an amazon.com gift card, DO NOT BUY THIS.-----EDIT 10-17-11-----I have harshly discredited both this and its 15w counterpart, and still don't recommend it, but I will be bumping both these amps up by 1 star. Here's why.It seems that the bluetooth audio receiver (Logitech Wireless Speaker Adapter for Bluetooth Audio Devices (980-000540)) I have been using was part of the problem. I just purchased a set of 2.0 speakers (Hercules XPS 2.0 30 Multimedia Speakers), and was having some (but not as much) distortion in my listening. I decided to try it out wired directly to my phone instead of wireless through bluetooth. As soon as the distortion vanished, I couldn't help but scream. I then proceeded to try the bookshelf speakers + Pyle amp again, and it was distorted as ever (due to the THD (total harmonic distortion) of 1% (this is very high, usually 0.1% is acceptable). I tried using it without the bluetooth adapter, and there was much improvement, but still more distortion with my $200 speakers than with the $50 hercules pair I'd just purchased. I'll still be returning the Pyle amp, but I'm crediting it one more star.

Update:  Within 6 months of easy use and cleaning, this developed a rip along the bottom seam.  The old one I mentioned below lasted much longer than this one.If you've never owned one of these foil filters then there are a couple things you should be prepared for up front.  First off, there will likely be some powder in the bottom of the pot with these filters.  There claim to fame is that they don't filter as much as paper--as they say it, they don't strip the oils that paper does, but they're still essentially saying they don't filter as well.  It should be obvious that something is likely to get past the foil screen that would not get through paper.  The second thing is that some of these say gold plated and some simply say gold.  Guess which is actually gold plated.  There can be a great quality difference between the low end and high end of pricing on these filters.  This is priced way up on the high end so your expectations of performance--how well if filters--and build quality--how long it will last--are well deserved.This is my second foil filter.  The last one had developed some tears after several years of use.  I always had some grounds/dust in the bottom of the pot with the old filter.  I've always felt it was a small price to pay to not have paper filters.Comparing this filter to the old one is tough since I've replaced the pot and grinder used with the old foil filter, but I have not found that there are any grounds in the pot with this filter.  Of course grind size and quality can have a big impact on this.There is at least one other comment complaining about the filter being hard to clean.  As you may well imagine, once you knock the grounds out into the trash can, or better yet, your garden, a simple rinse with a sprayer inside and from the outside through the screen will rinse the remaining grounds out.  I recommend a wipe with a towel or washcloth as well.  I also recommend that you clean the filter the same day you brew the pot.  We didn't do that reliably with the old filter and and you could tell after a few years.

The Logitech Quickcam Fusion is a nicely-designed piece of hardware right down to the unique 'tail' that lets it sit on the screen of pretty much any laptop. Once you go past design, though, you enter into some very dark and troubled waters.The hardware is a gem but the software is big, inefective and troublesome. This software never installed correctly. Its installer was meant to go in before the camera was ever attached but the actual installation crashed and I rebooted and tried it again. The second and all later attempts to install the thing excluded the original installer and went through some other process. The camera did actually work at this point so you think this is no problem. Then you actually *use* the camera and things become more wonderful from there.Other reviewers have praised this device for its picture quality, I personally was unimpressed by it. Despite the hype and the high price, I found that it was a webcam and only a webcam. It took a cold, if decent picture picture of whatever was in front of it: it did *not* transport you to shangri-la. Making it's ordinariness more noticable was the fact that the software wasn't done demonstrating how bad it was.While giving the cam a shot, I started noticing softwares I had no idea about cropping up and making themselves known--up to an including some sort of debugging utility I'd never heard of that showed up during shut-downs and other operations. Better still, the cam comes bundled with a utilities suite that allows various images to be drawn over your face by software that requires that you have a really powerful computer with tons of ram and top of the line video circuitry--pretty much the antithesis of a laptop. Maybe that was what it required, maybe it was something else. I never found out because I never once got it working and with all the previous problems of the softare installation as possible culprits, I certainly never found out why.In conclusion, you can say the Logitech Quickcam Fusion webcam is from a physical and esthetically well-designed camera, but one that as a package could be held up as a negative example in a class on business. You can almost imagine a professor saying it:"In a market crowded with less expensive and simpler-to-use alternatives, this is exactly what you are not supposed to do."

I had two main reasons for buying this; first so that I could compare two software apps at the same time and secondly so that when I am running presentations I can have the second screen for my notes. I have a Dell E6410 running Win7SP1 64 bit with 8Gb RAM with a standard inbuilt Intel Graphics driver. At work and home I have a second full size monitor. So what I was looking for a small portable unit to use when on customer sites.When I arrived I thought they'd sent the wrong device because it had `touch screen' on the box. But it seems they use the same box for both the UM-70 and the UM-70/C/T. I did not want the touch version.On opening, the first thing I did - amazing for a bloke - was look at the (minimal) instructions with incredibly small print. What caught my eye was the statement that Win7 64 bit was not supported. No other review seems to have mentioned this little tidbit of information. But others had said that it does work on 64 bit so I was bit confused by this. So I plugged it in and immediately W7 recognized the device and went out and downloaded the driver. Sometime last year MS updated their support site by adding the 5.6.31854.0 driver (the driver on the CD seems to be back at 5.2.xxx). Low and behold it worked. Screen is very bright as reported and amazingly sharp. It is a little small for what I really need but it's a case of matching form over function. I am not really using it for video, although I tried that and had no problems, but mainly for predominantly static screens. It certainly is great as a second screen for having things like your IM, email, music or other support apps running. And with a second VGA attached to the laptop I have 3 screens. They provide a `Y' USB cable for older or less powerful devices where a second USB port is required to provide adequate power. I do not need it.Now the problem. The screen keeps randomly freezing. In the forlorn hope that there may be one company out that can actually pronounce and spell `service', I sent Lilliput an email asking for advice. I'm still waiting. So off to the usual solution these days - Google and other self-help via forums. But no real joy their either. DisplayLink had a thread that talks about a variation of this issue but no solution documented. Some talk about aero being enabled but I have that on so don't think that is real root cause. So in the end I went to DisplayLink and downloaded the latest 6.1.35912 driver and installed that. So far the freeze seems to have gone but now the device periodically seems to need to reconnect and refresh.So the jury is still out for me. I'll see how it works for the next week or so. I don't know if this is the issue with the 64 bit support or not.  So while this is a great little support device, it has some issues. The other thing is that while they do not provide a case at this price, I think it would be nice if they at least provided a soft-cloth bag.If anyone else out there can provide comments on whether they have resolved these screen refresh / freeze issue, I'm sure that would be appreciated by all. If that were resolved this would get 4 starts, 5 if they provided a cover. Until then only 3. I'll update this review after a further period of use. Current ownership, 2 weeks.

You still have the battery issue mentioned by others, the audio quality is good, but not great, and they're not that comfortable.Look for a 5ghz capable setup, perhaps one of the more gaming oriented ones. We have a large office and warehouse, and much of the interior of the office space did not have cellular reception.  Those offices with windows were fine, but interior offices and cubes would get 1 bar or no service at all.  After extensive research, we chose this product due to the fact that we have excellent signal coverage outside our building which is the key to this unit.  If you do not have good cellular coverage from where your external antenna is mounted, then the device will have no way to relay any coverage to the inside of your building.We chose the directional antenna version because we can see the towers in our area and we were able to point the antenna directly at the nearest cell tower (there is also an omni-directional antenna option if you are located within sight of several cell towers).  Mounting of the external directional antenna was fairly easy, and once we ran the coax cable inside the rest of the installation was quick and straightforward.The key to this product is to make sure you attenuate the signal booster power correctly on the control unit.  If you have too much boost, you will not get good results.  Follow the directions carefully and attenuate both boosters until the LEDs just turn green (from red).  Once both LEDs are green you should have significantly increased cellular coverage inside your building area where the internal panel antenna is mounted.Most of our employees have AT&T;, but some are Verizon.  Both seem to benefit, although the AT&T; phones seem to get the biggest boost from this unit.  Phones located within 100' of the internal panel antenna have gone from no service / 1 bar to 4 or 5 bars of voice and full data signal strength.Overall we are very pleased with the outcome of this purchase. My husband and I purchased this vacuum back in December 2013 as a Christmas present for ourselves because we have two cats and recently has our first baby and were having trouble keeping up with the vacuuming, in spite of having lots of mess makers in the household.  We decided to go with the Neato because it was cheaper than the Roomba and was rated fairly highly here on Amazon... big mistake!  It's now 6 months later that I am writing this review and we are currently on our 4th replacement vacuum and it's now breaking down as well!  The first vacuum started having battery issues almost right off the bat.  The company sent us replacement batteries, but those batteries had has the same issues and the vacuum started having some other problem, I think it would just randomly shut down in the middle of cleaning without displaying any error message. So, Neato sent us a "refurbished" vacuum, which had problems right out of the box.  I think that particular refurbished vacuum wasn't able to dock with it's charging station and also had battery issues.  So, Neato sent us yet another "refurbished" vacuum.  This refurbished vacuum also had problems right out of the box, it kept displaying an error message saying that its brush was stuck.  At this point, it became clear that the refurbished vacuums that they were sending us really hadn't been fixed at all and Neato must have realized this, because they sent us another new vacuum (this time they upgraded our vacuum to the Neato XV Signature Pro, I guess because of all the trouble).  Now, we've had this last vacuum for a couple months and it has started having all sort of problems.  First, I noticed that the dust bin would keep popping up randomly during operation, causing the vacuum to shut down and display an error message.  Then, more recently it's started shutting down and displaying an error message that says, "Please clear my path" even when there is nothing in its path! Finally, the last straw was today when I tried to have the vacuum clean my entry way, it would just sit in one spot running, but not moving or displaying an error message.  We've contacted Neato yet again to try and straighten this out.  The worst part about dealing with all of these returns is that we keep having to send them copies of our invoice each time we contact them and then they try to make us troubleshoot and fix the vacuum ourselves (they'll often suggest things like resetting the batteries, unplugging the machine and restarting it, or emptying the dust bin, which of course we've already tried before contacting them).  The problem isn't that we're morons, the problem is that they are producing very glitchy products and have terrible quality control. At this point, I wish we could get our money back and buy a Roomba instead.

I see many posts on this and other sites about running mem chips above the rated speed for the processors listed. Some work and some don't - qvl's don't seem to have much to do with consistent outcomes, board or mem qvl's for that matter. You will be hard put to find an processor based imc that is rated to run memory properly (AMD/Intel- ddr2 or ddr3) above the rated imc of 800  1066. I think the I7 extreme is the only exception and even that stops at 1333 if I remember correctly. At least to run it stable and particularly if you try more then three chips (assuming six slots). Unfortunately, taking mem control from the FSB may have cheapened board costs, at least to the manufacturer :-), but imc's are falling further and further behind chip speeds without alot of fancy dancing in bios. This just one more bottleneck in a long and illustrious hx of bottlenecks in the land of PC's. When Intel and AMD publish rated imc specs they specify running above 800/1066 could be unstable (read that probably be unstable) and the bump up in performance is negligible.  So perhaps it is wise to stop paying top dollar for ram that does not run properly outside imc specs. IMHO

I just purchased these Vmoda Octave IEMs from a special deal at NewEgg.com ($15), and have been putting them through their paces for the last few days.  My test gear is (1) a Motorola Droid X2 with a player which allows FLAC files, and a Sansa Clip running either 16 bit FLAC or 320kbps MP3s. I switch between neutral EQ, or none at all.These IEMs have big swings in performance pending on which selection of ear inserts you choose - the larger the silicon tips, the worse/more boomy/less controlled the bass becomes. Overall, the sound is inoffensive, but not particularly accurate - highs are rolled off and indistinct, not airy and sharp; mids are same, and bass is volume attenuated, but never sharp. There's clearly a designed "bump" at lower frequencies to make them appear more "bassy".  In comparison testing, these are close to the latest JVC Marshmallows, but not as accurate.  They sound thin, flat and dimensionless compared to my reference Koss Portapros. At least they aren't bright and fatiguing, but they can't be accused of being great, or even good, with clean, hi resolution sources.Inoffensive and low cost, and they appear to be well made, but if you want better balance and resolution for comparable cost, there are lots of superior alternatives.

The short story is the EZ-Cup works GREAT for people wanting to use their own coffee and save money. Don't waste your money on any non-paper reusable filters - the coffee will be weak and full of sediment without a paper filter.I considered buying a Keurig coffee maker for over a year. I was getting tired of cleaning all of the coffee pot parts and built in grinder every day; usually in the morning when I really wanted a cup of coffee - fast. I was delighted with how easy and quick the Keurig machine was. I really wanted to use my own coffee and keep my costs down, so I also purchased a reusable filter with a metal mesh type filter. I was SO disappointed. The coffee was weak and full of sediment which you can taste even before you get to the bottom of the cup.After doing some research on Amazon and taking apart a K-Cup, I discovered three things: 1.) A paper filter was the answer (the inside of a K-Cup has a paper filter), 2.) I should grind the coffee to the same consistency as the coffee in a K-Cup and 3.) Don't PACK your coffee tightly into these filters or the water may not be able to infuse the coffee properly and you may have a mess on your hands if the water can't penetrate the pod you are using.The problem with the reusable single cup filters with a metal mesh is the hot water runs through these non-paper filters too quickly and produces a very weak cup of coffee. Also, coffee ground with home grinders creates super fine particles that get through the mesh filters and into your cup. The sediment leaves a bad taste. A paper filter slows the hot water down just enough to strengthen the taste AND it filters out the sediment. I have 3 cups size settings on my Keurig. The middle 7.25 oz setting is perfect for me. The 9.25 oz is always too weak for me.Some people say coffee run through a paper filter is healthier than coffee run through a non-paper filter because it filters out bad things. I do know it tastes MUCH better.I researched all of the paper filters and decided to try the Ez-Cup and Ez-Cup filters based on reviews and because it had Amazon Prime shipping. They cost from around .10 - .125 cents each, which is great. I found it very easy and quick to make up a "pod." Fill the filter to the top with coffee, place it in the Ez-Cup plastic pod, flip the paper filter top across the top, then press the plastic lid down to seal, drop it in the machine and go.I read about one person adjusting the spring lower to get more coffee in the filter for a stronger cup of coffee. After studying the Ez-Cup for awhile, I did not see how it was possible to adjust the spring. I didn't want to ruin my new pod, so I called Ez-Cup customer service and they said I did not need to make any adjustments to get a full filter of coffee. When you place a paper filter in the Ez-Cup, about  of it will project above the top of the Ez-Cup. That's okay. Fill the filter all the way to the top of the paper with coffee. You can fill the filter while holding it in your hand or set it in the Ez-cup and fill it all the way to the top. (Ok to shake it to level while filling, but do not tamp it down.) I gently flick any coffee I may have gotten on the outside edges of the filter so there's no coffee between the seal, flip the paper top over, press the lid down and it will compact the filter into the cup against the spring loaded bottom and seal shut.Unlike what some other reviews said, I found it easy to press the plastic lid on. If it's new and a little tight, set it on the counter and press down with the ball of your hand. After one cup, the plastic warms up and is VERY easy to press down for a second cup.If there was a filter breakage issue in the past, there is not now. I went through 200 filters with no problem.I highly recommend the Ez-Cup and Ez-Cup filters!

When buying bookshelf speakers for my surround system my wife had one requirement. They had to be white - I however had a few more criteria.1 - Sound - Always the number 1 priority for speakers. Midrange performance is solid - never muffled - and you are treated with crisp high notes as high as your ears will alloy you to hear!2- Durability - I have had the speakers for about 4 years with no problems. I like the fact that they are a hard-shell plastic as it makes them a little tougher than the old wood encased speakers.3- Works well outdoors - mind you I would not leave these things directly exposed to a downpour, but they should be ok if exposed to some humidity.4- Weight - a little on the heavy side - not bad - certainly not as bad as my big honking floorspeakers, but they weigh about 10lbs a piece. This means it is a bit of a chore if are continuously moving these things from indoors to out. It also means that you need to be careful if you decided to mount them to your walls - you will definitely need to either hit a stud or use screw anchors.Final Verdict - A nice value for the price - the offer good (but not great) sound and can be used indoors and out!4 Stars

இ Fuzzy Wuzzy's Summary:ѾѾѾѾ Recommended with warm fuzzies for Skype use.  For music or gaming use, you are far better off using other headphones or microphone headsets.Use of this headset for gaming or listening to music on your computer is pretty simple.  You just plug it into a USB port, it auto-installs its device driver on Windows, and you are ready to go.  For use with Skype, along with having Skype downloaded and installed on your computer, you download additional software from Plantronics' Web site that will let you customize the headset's usage characteristics, your mute tone, change your ring settings, manage your Media Player settings using the software's control panel, and you can answer or end Skype calls by simply pushing a button the inline control panel that is connected onto the headset's USB cord.  Note that both the downloadable software and the Skype call answer/end feature are only available to Windows users, and not to Mac users.This headset comes with a 6-foot cable that makes it convenient to connect to the rear of a desktop computer, but if you are just using it on a laptop, you may want to leave the twist tie that is wrapped around the bundled-up cord.The included foldout instruction sheet says that the 32mm-diameter headphone speaker drives have a frequency response of "20Hz-20kHz", but to my ears, this headphone's sound is more focused in the mid-range frequencies, which constitute the bulk of human voice and speech, while the upper timbres of high frequencies do not have as much sparkle as some comparably-sized stereo headphones that are made for music.  Likewise, if you use this headset for video gaming or listening to music, the low-end frequency response does not play percussion and drums very powerfully.  The overall sound has a very nice warm tone to it, and with the upper frequencies attenuated, at least music that is played through these headphones does not sound strident compared to some small headphones that can over-emphasize the high frequencies.  The headset advertises that the "integrated equalizer ensures balanced, dynamic audio", so perhaps this integrated acoustically-tuned equalizer is shaping the sound more around the mid-range frequencies so that Skype calls sound great.  Listening to speech coming from NPR or talk radio also sounds good.  So this headset's sound is ideal for voice and speech.  But if you are wanting a gaming headset or if you want to use this headset to frequently listen to music, you may be disappointed by the more subdued high treble frequencies and the lack of good tight bass on this headset.  This headset's advertised "24-bit high-fidelity stereo output" may be contributing to its exemplary performance on Skype calls, but for playing either music or gaming audio, there are many other headphones and headsets that sound better for those two applications.When used with Skype, the headset's noise-canceling microphone works wonderfully; my calls and speech always come across crisp and clear to the person that I am speaking to.  I never, even once, had an issue with either static or echo with how my voice sounded.  Likewise, the other person's voice also sounded great through the headphones.Regarding the comfort of wearing this headset for an extended period, overall, I like it.  The soft ear pads that cover the headphones are very comfortable.  But you may either like or hate the behind-your-head design of this headset's headband.  The plastic that curves around the headphones sit on top of your earlobes and the headband goes out of sight behind your head.  With the headband hidden behind my head instead of wrapped on top of my head, I like the idea that I do not look so much like a "Hi I'm Janet from Time-Life Books, may I take your order?" telephone operator whenever I am on Skype.  Some people also like a behind-the-head headband design because it does not mess up their hair.  Your mileage may vary.  But this headband is on the small side and it is just a one-piece non-adjustable plastic curve.  If you either have a lot of hair volume or if the shape of the back of your head is larger than normal, this could make for a tight fit to position the headband around the rear of your head.  And probably because the headphones have to position themselves over your ears without the benefit of an over-the-head headband supporting them, these headphones do clamp onto your ears a bit tighter than many headsets based on over-the-head headbands.  I did not mind this, but I wear this headset for less than two hours during each Skype session, and it would have been far better if the headband was adjustable or some parts of the headband were bendable instead of being a single piece of curved plastic.  If the headband was made of a bendable metal and extended out behind the wearer's head more to accommodate larger heads or larger volumes of hair, people could then make slight adjustments and they could then mold the curved section that wraps around the top of their ears to get a better custom fit for their particular shape of ears and head.  If you prefer a headset with a more conventional over-the-head headband, thePlantronics Audio 478 Stereo USB Headset (Audio 478)is identical to this model 648 except for the headband design.Overall, this is a nice headset for use with Skype.  For its Skype performance and the headset's microphone performance, I would rate this 5 stars.  But I would rate both its non-adjustable headband and the headphone's suboptimal performance when playing music or gaming audio at 3 stars.  So my 4-star overall rating means "great for Skype use, assuming that the headband is comfortable for your head and ears", but not that good for music and gaming, and the headband should have been designed as a larger curve made of bendable rubber-coated metal.

I picked this up and mounted it on a Mossberg 500 tactical. It is a solid light, with good construction and very bright. The "LED" is actually a SMD, which accounts for the brightness. The beam adjustment really doesn't work very well, and it looks like it is due to the construction of the reflector in the beam housing. With that being said, it puts a pretty good beam downrange, and has very little scattered light. When I mounted the pressure switch pad, it didn't work, so I took apart the end cap, and found the problem. The two wires that connect to the PCB were not soldered very well, and were "held" in place with a small dab of hot glue. After soldering the wires back on properly, and filling it in with epoxy, the swith works great. The pressure pad only requires a small ammount of pressure, and is easily mounted to the handguard of the Mossberg. the wire coils are pretty long, so they should be able to mount on even the longest barrel, but being mounted on a short barrel (18 inch) the coils are a bit too long. The light has held up to rain, dirt, and about 500 rounds so far, without a single failure. Its a tough lamp, that is lightweight, and has held up really well so far. If your willing to put a little work into it, its an inexpensive product that can rival the higher end lamps, for a third of the price! I am going to pick up another one for one of my AR rifles, and see how it holds up.

This is a review for the Newegg product (May differ from the Amazon product).I scoured the Internet for hours looking for the right graphics card to play BF3 among other games.  The graphics card I was looking for needed to be very high-end to warrant replacing my awesome little HD 7750.  A particular tool I found to be helpful was anandtech(dot)com/bench/GPU12/372.  It compares GPUs results in MANY tests they performed.  They also post SLI/CrossFire results for some cards.The GTX 660 and the GTX 660Ti performed very similarly, definitely not enough to warrant another $70.  The 660 also has INSANE SLI scaling.  Two 660s in SLI perform better than one 680 that costs about $40 more in the end.  The GTX 670 is possibly the worst video card from Nvidia.  It is VERY comparable to an overclocked 660Ti with a non-reference cooler, but it costs $100 more.  A GTX 650 is too low-end for my needs and doesn't even beat my 7750.  I knew I had to get the 660.  Oh yeah, I was looking at an HD 7850, but at the last moment the price jumped from $185 to $215.Now that I knew I wanted a GTX 660, I needed to figure out which manufacturer to purchase from.  I hate Gigabyte motherboards and I proudly show off my awesome MSI motherboard to everyone.  I wanted an MSI Power Edition or Twin Frozer III GTX 660.  I found one for the exact same price as this Gigabyte.  Even though I hate Gigabyte's motherboards, I love their Windforce coolers on graphics cards.  My 7750 could be turned up to 100% speed and all you heard was the whooshing of air.  The fan bearing must be pretty good to hear no noise from the fan spinning.  Gigabyte fans are also larger (About 90mm) and that means they move more air than smaller fans (Like on MSI's) and at a lower noise level.  MSI's TWIII fans are supposedly "Impeller blade fans", but to me they just look tiny and noisy, much like a really old 8400GS I had once that just couldn't keep quiet.  The blue and black Gigabyte color scheme also matches my MSI mobo very well :P  If you haven't tried either brand's custom graphics cards cooler, I'd recommend using MSI's just to try it out because I hear it works very well.  I decided to do the tried and true Gigabyte Windforce skew.  It works well enough anyway and I got fairly high overclocks.  I'm not going to share them with you because every GPU and memory module is different and can sustain higher overclocks.  I don't want anyone to damage their GPU because they saw someone else achieve those results.  Sometimes you can only get 10-20MHz, and sometimes you can get hundreds of MHz.

In Client mode the WAP3205 is locked in "mixed 802.11n/g/b mode". This means your router must also be in mixed mode else you get a red check-mark in the Pofile List (sic) instead of the green check mark that you want to see and the WAP won't connect, (not sure why they use a check-mark to indicate an error condition, it's only half broken at this point I guess). Anyhoo, with router & WAP both in mixed mode the WAP connects fine, but the connection is 802.11g so you only get max speed of 24 Mbps, not the 300 MBps (you'll be lucky) that you got an 'n' WAP for in the first place. Transferring a 66Mb file through the ZyXel took 108s, but only 42s using an Airport Express we also have hanging around that does make an 'n' connection (even though it too only does mixed mode). Maybe it's an issue between the ZyXel and my DIR-655 router but the D-Link's a pretty popular, and good, router so I know which one stays and which one goes of these 2. I wonder if others who are reporting "no problems" are checking to see what mode/speed they're getting, many seem to be using WEP rather than WPA/WPA2 which suggests they can only be getting 'g' because 'n' doesn't support WEP. I also tried using the ZyXel in Universal Repeater mode which gives you Client mode functionality but also gives you the Configuration -> Network -> Wireless LAN -> General -> Advanced tab that you need to change the 802.11 mode, but that still doesn't have an 'n' only option. The device now comes with a 204 page user guide on the CD, in places it's more like a WiFi primer than a basic user guide and makes for a great bedtime read, though all you really need to know about setup is in the top 2 Amazon reviews (1 1/2 pages).

There are two things a radar detector should do well: detect and alert. The testing sites give this detector high marks in detection. In my everyday driving, it seems accurate, alarming or keeping quiet when it should. I haven't had any laser, pop, or SWS alerts, just X, K, and Ka. So far, I've used only the AutoScan mode, and it works pretty well. "Detect" gets 4.5 stars."Alert" is not so good. The audible component is nice and loud, with an adjustable volume. The spoken voice alert is clear (sounds like the FLDSMDFR), sort of like a training mode to help you recognize the different beeps. The volume is a tad hard to adjust since you have to push and hold the button and wait for it to go all the way up before it goes down, or vice versa. On the plus side of that, though, you won't accidentally change the volume while handling it. My issue with the audible is when the signal is full-strength, the tones are still beeping somewhat slowly - not a "solid" tone - so it sounds more like a half-strength signal. My other issue is with the visual component, it's just not that noticeable. It uses the same display which displays the mode, so it doesn't stand out. If you miss the audible for whatever reason, the visual may not catch your attention. This should have a dedicated alert light (the smart cord doesn't count.) Or at least, they could do better with the existing display by auto-brightening the display and using full-height bars. "Alert" gets 2 stars.My other major dislike about this detector is the color - gray with light gray and shiny silver numbers on top - c'mon! This thing puts off a major reflection in the windshield which is distracting (polarized sunglasses help to minimize that.) And if you're trying to hide this on the floor of the car, cover it up - did I mention the shiny silver numbers? A radar detector should be only two colors - flat and black.As for other features, I like the programmable configuration. The quick-mount works well, but it leaves the suction cups on the windshield, which just invites trouble when parked. The laser alert goes off when I'm attaching it to the windshield, and that's annoying. The smart cord I find to be mostly useless. The alert light is small, and with most power sockets being out of the way, you just won't see it. It's got a mute button, but so does the main body. Some people complain about smart cords not being standard, but in this case I'd like it to be optional and save myself 20-30 bucks.

I suppose I am not the real target demographic for this speaker set.  It is pretty clearly aimed at those who want a modest, budget enhancement for gaming, whereas I am a music fan. However, the main speakers are not exactly audiophile equipment, so what you really get with this set is the ability to crank up the bass a bit so that there is a modest rumble with those explosions in games.  For music, the sound is only a modest improvement on the built-in speakers on my iMac desktop.  Frankly, I have no desire to crank up the bass while listening to Miles Davis, so without good treble, these speakers are not for me.  The other limiting factor to keep in mind is that the cables are rather short, meaning you won't have many options for speaker placement.  They are just long enough to keep the subwoofer at your feet underneath the desk with the main speakers to either side of your monitor.  For music, speaker placement matters far more, so you need to have longer cables.Is this for you?  That depends.  If you want a good listening experience for music, sorry, but you'll have to shell out more money.  If you just want a cheap set with a subwoofer for those games, then I suppose these might do, but don't expect miracles.

I got one at Weiss for $30.00+ tax--too good to be true but no signs of box having been opened. So far, a real steal. Upon opening box, noticed tiny dent in one side area, nothing to fuss about as you get what you pay for andno harm done to interior or finish--so for $30 over higher cost + shipping costs, it's still a deal. The SMOKE OUT, however, has been unbelievable! Another reviewer stopped at saying that as an apartment dweller the first use directions are ridiculous as they call for a carport or garage, well-ventilated, in which to perform the smoke out.I will add that one is allowed to use extension cords only if they match the electrical rating of the appliance. With that in mind, and feeling I could skip the recommended setting and extension cord, I took the thing into an empty large utility room with a tile floor and set it facing an open door to our back porch so air would circulate in and out of the room. The fumes smelled toxic the first hour and did not go away. If you try this, stick to "WELL ventilated"--meaning somehow out in the open air with windows surrounding the object if not in an open air carport or garage. I turned it off and let air leave room for most part and noticed that instructions say to smoke out for an hour "or" until the smoke smell is gone. Upon trying the foregoing routine again, I find I am now into the object's fourth hour of its second chance and the air is still nauseating and filled with toxic fumes likely, in my view, to kill the same small birds that nonstick coatings kill--which is why I ordered porcelain enamel coated cookwell to begin with! Seriously, I wonder how safe this product really will be to use later on? Will it always stink? Will I be poisoned thoroughly before the thing is through smoking out? And why isn't this process carried on in a factory where it is safer for others and the environment? While this may be a factory second given the dent,  I don't believe the appliance's heating is damaged. Evidentially Nesco knows the American consumer well. Seems most of us will put up with anything, including shoddy factory standards and work. Not keeping it. -- It is now one hour later and the smoke out has run a total of 6 hours (1 the first time and then 5 more) and the stench is still the same, not diminished. I suspect people stop it at one hour and wash it but cook food in it after that and perhaps assume there are no fumes every time they turn it on and cook with it. I've turned it off and will wash it and see if this makes a difference before restarting it after it cools down. But regardless of outcome, all of this is a real hassle and a drawback to buying a roaster oven from Nesco, in my view.

I bought this as a replacement for a Sony RDR-GX300 that stopped playing all discs after five years of daily use.  The Toshiba DR570 meets my basic recording needs, but that's all. The Toshiba shows the first frame of the record, which isn't helpful given that it's always the commercial that aired before the program started.  Once you highlight the program, it does start to play in the preview pane and show the time and date it was recorded but it'd be nice to know immediately like I did with the Sony.The remote is definitely the worst one I've experienced.  It's hard to read in low light and doesn't have many of the buttons I expected.  There's no volume control, tv/video (it instead switches between the analog and digital tuners for the recorder), or record stop and pause buttons.Another annoyance with this machine is the inability to create a new record or modify an existing one while watching what you've recorded.  The Sony allowed me to do that as did all the VCRs I previously used.  Furthermore, you lose program audio when you're setting up a record.I'm using the same discs I used with the Sony (Memorex +RWs) that never led to any coasters before now.  The Toshiba doesn't always like to fully erase the program.  Luckily, it does tell you that deleting the title will not create additional free space.  I've discovered a workaround for this.  Don't delete the title, play a few seconds of it, then go back in to delete.  It doesn't come up with the message about not giving me back the space and the machine continues to record on the disc after that.

I have owned a Canon TX and Canon 650 film cameras.  I was always very happy with my Canon film cameras.  I bought the 10d thinking that I was finally able to get a digital replacement for my old Canon film cameras.I have now owned my 10d for over a year.  The picture quality is only fair.  It often selects ISO 100 and gives me fuzzy pictures. The white balance is extremely poor compared with the film cameras.  The "full automatic" mode does a poor job of focus and white balance.  The "creative" modes are similar to the film cameras but don't seem to work so very well.  I am just having a terrible time trying to get the settings right to get good pictures!  After a year of trying I am extremely frustrated with it.Finally, the print pictures I get from it are _always_ too dark.  It seems I need to post-process EVERY PICTURE in photoshop to get the gamut correct, or brighten/enhance/correct the photos to make them look right.  Argh!It's all probably user error, but I never had these problems with my old film cameras.  If I could easily get PhotoCDs made I would go back to film immediately!UPDATE:  Okay, I bought PhotoShop CS for my Mac.  I have taken some of my old 10d photos and run this sequence:Auto LevelsAuto Brightness/ContrastSaturation +30 (variable)Unsharpen Mask (this one takes the most tweaking)This has _really_ made a huge difference in the quality of the photos.  I have done a lot more adjustment with some of the photos.  Photoshop is _really_ amazing what it can do.  The image have a _lot_ of info in them, I just have to learn to get it to pop out.

These handsome Philips CitiScape Uptown headphones blast out the bass like I haven't heard in a long time. For an iPod or iPhone, this is not a horrible thing, but for any other source, it is almost impossible to dial down the bass to a comfortable level. If you love bass, if you love Dr. Dre, if you love hip hop, these are the most fantastic headphones in the world. If you are looking for accurate clear sound, look elsewhere.Philips CitiScape series of headphones are some of the nicest looking, comfortable headphones around. These cans are incredibly comfortable. They fit all the way over my ear, sealing sound from leakage and cushioning me in just the right amount of blessed silence (in ear monitors are far better at sealing out external noise, these do a good job). The ear cushions are the softest memory foam and the headband is perfectly padded. My big pointy head loves these headphones (in fact I normally pull headphones all the way to full extension, not these).I really like this color combination, the chocolate headband, the matte silver ear cups, white cushions, and the brown flat cable; all look great together. Construction appears to be pretty darn solid. There are two steel wires that connect the two earpieces. Each ear cup gimbals nicely to conform to my head.The volume control / microphone plug is one of the worst. The button simply controls stop start on an iPhone. The volume slider is just that, a volume slider limiter; it does not change the device volume. I really hate this kind of arrangement; it adds resistance to the circuit, another place to pick up nasty sounds. If Philips uses a cheap resistor in the volume limiter (and they probably did given the miniscule size of the control) that resistor will add noise to the headphones. The slider is also way too easy to slide; I've inadvertently changed the volume level.The jack is an odd little beast. The plug is 90 degrees, short and fat. I have a very deep phone case that prevents the jack from working. If you have a deep case, either buy an extension cord or different headphones.Notice, I wrote about the look and feel of these headphones before the all so critical sound evaluation. In my view, these are just way too bass heavy. I tried these out on an iPod shuffle, and an iPhone 4s; the results were the same - highs were rolled off, lyrics were hard to understand, the bass was boosted significantly, the soundstage was a muddy blurry mess, and it was very difficult to define any of the instruments. I did some back to back comparisons of V-Moda M-80's and Philips less expensive CitiScape Downtown over ear headphones. Both were infinitely clearer and sharper. Granted the V-Modas are about $50 more expensive, but the Philips Downtowns are $50 cheaper and put out better sound.Philips Accessories SHL5605BK/28 CitiScape Downtown Headphones (Black)Beats by Dr. Dre Solo HD White On-Ear Headphone from MonsterV-MODA Crossfade M-80 On-Ear Noise-Isolating Metal Headphone (Shadow)The overboosted bass was all too evident when I hooked these headphones up to a stereo (Pro-Ject turntable, NAD preamplifier, NAD integrated stereo amplifier). With bass turned to the lowest level possible and treble up all the way, the headphones still vibrated with too much bass. Bass can be a good thing when it is clear and well defined. Bass is a bad thing when it just thumps and is muddy, or when it intrudes on the vocals. I will admit one very positive thing, at incredibly high volume, the headphones actually output some nice sound (I turned up the amplifier about 3/4 of the way and wrapped the headphones around my neck, but not over my ears).What confounds me with these headphones; they use the exact same driver as the less expensive Downtown headphones, a 40mm speaker. The cavity for these Uptown speakers must resonate at a really wrong frequency and cause all kinds of trouble with the rest of the sound spectrum. It is so hard to believe these two headphones are from the same manufacturer.My frame of reference for headphones is very wide, from Bowers & Wilkins (P5 and C5) and V-Moda Crossfades (LP and M-80) to SkullCandy Titans and JLab II. I love audio and headphones.So you love bass, are these good headphones? Well they are $25 cheaper than Dr. Dre, and they both put out just as much bass in the exact same fashion. If you tend to follow the crowd, that Beats logo is worth every penny of $25. However, if you like to be unique and do things a little different, these Philips headphones are just the ticket.Personally I prefer my headphones to be very accurate, so these just don't work for me. They do have just enough sound isolation to work on an airplane. And they make great action movie headphones. They are super comfortable and look darn nice. I just wish they sounded better.

My main draw to a netbook, next to portability, was something with strong battery life that would allow me to remain productive when out & about.  The smaller size is appealing not only because it is easy to tote around the house, or around town, but also because it is easy to work on while flying (in economy, the small space is often too cramped to use even my 13.3" notebook, but this works out great).  The HP 110 mini is one of many new netbooks on the market, and it is certainly one of the most attractive with the sleek black cover with design on it.  Performance with XP Home and the standard 1 GB of memory has been just fine.  Battery life on this has been fairly good.  I've used only with the wi-fi on, but have still had no problems geting 5 hours.  Someone commented on the large battery that sticks out.  This is true, and definitely affects how you might store this. Most netbook sleeves won't work because of how the battery juts out perpendicularly.  On the plus side, I find the battery serves as a nice hand-hold for carrying the computer around.  I actually feel much more secure carrying it this way.  And this design tilts the keyboard for more ergonomic typing as well.  The screen is decent on this -- comparable to what I've found on other netbooks.  So there is plenty to like.  Where I really get frustrated with the HP 110 mini, however, is the cramped keyboard.  After several days, I'm still not totally at ease typing on it, even with my small hands.  Using the touchpad buttons is also really awkward.  I have yet to understand why the buttons run vertically on the left & right sides of the touchpad instead of side by side along the bottom.  This really limits productivity, which is a main reason I got this.  I was also not impressed at all with the quality of the webcam.  Given that most features on netbooks (memory, OS, hard drive, wi-fi, etc.) are fairly standard, you'd be better off looking at the new Asus 1005HA-P, which has similar specs but 10.5 hour battery life AND a keyboard that is actually a delight to use.

Although billed as "Ultra high speed USB 2.0", the negotiated USB bus speed is actually 12 mbits/s.  Which USB standard calls "full" speed.  It *is* a USB 2.0 device, and reports as such on the bus, it just doesn't support the higher bus speed.  One normally expects USB 2.0 storage devices to use the 480 mbits/s bus speed, and with current class 10 SD devices supporting 30 mbytes/s (*bytes*, not bits), the device is hopelessly inadequate.  It can't even handle  yesteryears class 6 SD devices properly (6 Mbytes/s).However, at a buck each including shipping, the price is right, and it seems to operate reliably.  I'm not even mad that I still have to buy another device that I can actually use.  If speed doesn't matter for your application, this is the cheap way to go.Note, the standard shipping uses USPS which is having problems these days.  The envelope was postmarked Oct 11, and it was delivered Oct 28.  If you need them right away, get the faster shipping (at which point you might as well get a more expensive device).  So if neither speed of operation nor speed of delivery matter for your applications, this is the cheap way to go.

(Recharging my iPhone 5 took about same time under the same condition). It took about 4 hours to recharge my iPad retina model from 0% to slightly under 50% and then the Power Bank’s battery was exhausted. I tried this again the next day, and it only charged 26% (from 0%) and it took 2 hours, then soon after the Power Bank’s battery exhausted.My thoughts on this battery pack is mixed, and I am slightly disappointed. It is wonderful that this pack can charge almost two iPhones from zero to full without any wall plugged power, but at the same time, it couldn’t handle my iPad. The product description shows ‘Other Smartphones and Tablets’, but the ‘tablet’ portion probably applies only to some smaller-sized tablets with smaller capacity battery.I did, however, like how it is designed. It worked conveniently well with my existing Powermat (I didn’t have to plug anything to recharge this battery pack), and it offers two different USB ports (regular and mini). The size is small like a portable hard drive and weight is lighter than my iPhone 4s. I had plenty of incidents where my phone died out of battery during trips. So an extra battery pack is a must have for me when traveling. Although, the price of this battery pack is quite high, its high capacity will serve some high conveniences during future trips.

I have used them about 10 times now and I still have not found that it repels humidity.  I have fairly thick, straight hair about 1-2" past my shoulders.Pros:Unlike some other brands, EACH hair roller came with it's own clip.The rollers & clips heat up FAST.  Mfg claims it heats up in 90 seconds and I'd have to agree.The rollers are 'coated' with velvet so that the part that touches your hair is gentle on it.The set contains PLENTY of rollers in the larger size, which I generally prefer...it has a total of 20 rollers...8 medium ( 1") rollers and 12 large rollers ( 1 1/4").Perhaps it's the tourmaline in the rollers but I do think that it made my hair a SMIDGE (so minute that only I noticed) shinier.It has a cord storage compartment so your cord won't be left dangling everywhere.CONS:The entire unit is BIG for storage.  Most other mfgs make the unit so that it's longer in length but slimmer in width.  This Remington TStudio  H-2050 set is not only long in length but also in wide in it's width AND since the rollers are displayed in a 'stadium type' arrangement, it's also much taller on it's highest point than other brands.  So for those who prefer to store their hair roller sets under their sink, in  a drawer or in a cabinet of some sort, the height of this set may be an issue for storage.  I found no benefit except a visual appeal of having this set designed so 'tall'.  I have a basket underneath my vanity in which I store my hair rollers, curling iron, straightener, hair dryer, etc.  With my older hair roller set, I stored it on the bottom - the first layer in the basket with my hair styling equipment.  I can't do that with this one and have everything LOOK organized as much as nothing will lay flat on the top cover because it's slanted.As much as I wanted to LOVE this set, the most important reason for using hair rollers is so that it will give your hair body...whatever style you are trying to achieve...this set has never held the shape in my hair.  I've tried both the medium & large rollers, I've tried heating it up for longer, leaving them in for longer and for some reason, the shape and body just won't hold as long.  (I have a theory that I will include below.)One of my 2 largest complaints about this product is the fact that since the clips get HOT, someone in the design department forgot to coat / layer the top of the clips with some sort of coating or substance that would not heat up as hot as the rollers.  I'm not a wimp...I've burned myself a jillion times from VERY HOT curling irons but sheesh, you figure when the rollers are IN your hair, you shouldn't have to tilt your head from side to side because the HOT clips are burning the tips of your ears, your cheekbone, your cheek, etc.  I found that using this set has not saved me time because I use the rollers on one side of my head at a time so I can tilt my head a bit while I put on my makeup so it doesn't burn my skin.My MAJOR complaint about this set are the darn CLIPS.  I can't imagine why in the world a company would design and manufacture hair clips that are SMOOTH?  There are absolutely no teeth, no spikes, no rubber (not that I'd want warm or hot 'rubber' on my hair) at all to HOLD ONTO or grip your hair.  So no matter how tight and how well you roll your hair up with these rollers, the clips lack the 'grip' it would take to hold onto your hair to create long lasting waves or curls in your hair since they will be certain will slip - at least a little after you 'clip' the roller onto your hair.  I've tried and tried to establish a good grip and no matter what, it always slips an inch or two at minimum after I've let go.I have not yet experienced the 'bend' in your hair like some other reveiwers have so I can't comment on that except to say that I personally have had smooth curls or waves when I first release my hair from the rollers.If I had to purchase these, I personally would not be happy with this set mainly because of how the clips have no 'grip' in them and how uncomfortable they are when they are in my hair.  I'm not thrilled about how wide & tall this set is but that's something that I could manage to live with if I really loved this set.  I think if Remington simply redesigned their clips then it would be a pretty decent set. (Remington: perhaps you would design some different clips for those of us who would love to have an option for clips that grip your hair?)  For that main reason, I am sorry but I simply can't give this product a GREAT rating.With that said, I realize that reviewers here don't have qualms about the clips (although I cannot understand why) so if you think you'd be able to manage or tolerate the clips and you only want waves (not curls) in your hair, then you may like this set a lot.  I DO like how this made my hair a little smoother and shinier.  My hair does not feel dry at all after using these rollers and that in itself is an advantage.

At 11:30 last night, this tracker said that I slept for 21 minutes. I'm sure my clients wouldn't be very happy to hear that I was asleep while I was, in fact, working on the computer during those 21 minutes. Similarly, when I stay in bed listening to music or just arguing with myself to get the heck up, it often records that I'm still asleep, which throws off my readings. Occasional errors are to be expected, but I'd like to be able to manually override this information. There is no way to do that at the moment.I've also found heart rate readings to be questionable. The pedometer is generally accurate, especially once you get into a "rhythm," but sometimes when I start walking or jogging, it hiccups-- once it started counting by twos! (But straightened out quickly.)However!I think the advanced sleep tracker is very cool, as it gave me some insights over the course of several days that made sense to me. I was trying to figure out whether or not I'm getting enough "quality" sleep. I know I sleep enough hours, yet I'm still tired pretty often, so I was trying to figure out what's going on. What I found was that I get practically no deep sleep when my daughter is in my room (which is most nights). Then, when she leaves for school and I take a nap, *wham!* Straight to deep sleep. It made sense to me because she tosses and turns, which must prevent me from getting into deep sleep.I like the habits, but don't like that I have to "earn" the right to choose new habits. It's fun in theory, but I want to be a grownup and choose what I want to choose.The watch is bulky (understandable, considering what's going on inside), which makes it a little awkward for a petite woman like me to wear. After seeing a reviewer mention that it was not water-resistant after all, I haven't tried wearing it in the shower to test this.I'm frustrated that the tracker goes right back to the clock after a few seconds when you check something like heart rate or steps. When I'm walking, I'd like the default to be that it continues to show me the steps taken, not that I have to keep pressing the button to see that information.The display is very dark unless you hit the backlight, and then it gets better but still not bright. Not sure why it can't be better illuminated all the time like a typical digital watch.Battery life hasn't been a problem. I charge it when I take a shower and it stays charged just fine.A bonus: My daughter (age 7) wanted to use it and I didn't expect it to be accurate on such a little wrist. It was! It fit on the tightest setting and showed her that she entered REM sleep 7 times throughout the night. She thought it was very cool to have "7 dreams" per night. :)All in all, I love the possibilities of this tracker, and it's been a real game-changer for me to see my stats every day and know that I still have a long way to go to hit a healthier lifestyle (my job is sedentary). There's room for improvement, and I hope Basis makes it.

I have a Dell Studio XPS 9000 with a 64-bit operating system. My old, trusty, easy-to-use UPS will only work on this system as a surge protector but not as a battery back up (which is what gives you a few minutes to find a stopping point, save your documents and properly shut down Windows). So I purchased two of these units (one for me and one for my sister-in-law's new computer.)If you're used to the regular UPS interface which has a Personal Power Chute interface window that provides all the system information you need by just clicking on the icon, this one is different. There is no user interface other than the panel on the front of the unit which gives you a lot of information but not all you'd like. All that information (minutes her system can keep running without a/c power, etc.) is now provided online--which explains why you need a password.I'm not too sure that I like this system because, in case of a serious weather emergency the modem may not work and I wouldn't have access to information I'd need in the short time that the computer will be running. I like the computer-based system a lot better for an individual computer. I have the feeling that this system, while it will work with individual home computers, is really designed for networks and workplaces.The first installation was flawless, everything worked right away, and the unit was recognized by the web interface and all the system information was provided.The second installation, performed exactly in the same sequence, went fine until I tried to connect to the web interface and was told this was an "unknown device" and no information could be provided about it. This is a little unnerving because I have no confirmation that it is properly configured and will work in an emergency. So, at this point, I'm waiting for the reply to my e-mail service request.I tried to find information to help me solve the problem in the user manual (on cd) without any success. The book is not written for a lay person.  You get terms such as "name string outlet group," "switched outlet group", and "normally closed contacts"  which probably make sense to an IT professional, but don't mean anything to me. I can't see anything on the manual that could address my problem (of course, heaven only knows what creative name my problem might have).I am giving this product three stars because, due to my previous experience with APC tech support, I'm pretty confident that this glitch will get straightened out. (I will update if it doesn't). Also, my sister-in-law's unit is working beautifully. Besides, it is the only reasonably-priced smart ups I could find and it has the capacity to protect the five items that I've plugged into it: the CPU, two monitors, a scanner, and an external hard drive and still am at a 48% load capacity.However, I'm deducting one star for the layout of the outlets. They are so closely spaced that, unless you're plugging in just ordinary sized plugs, you lose at least one (maybe even two) of the six available outlets because you just can't jam another in between the chunky plugs that come with scanners, CPU's, etc. (Let alone if you should want to plug in an external hard drive that comes with one of those little adapter boxes!) I wasn't able to plug in the printer, not because of lack of load capacity but because of lack of space.I'm also deducting one star for the software.  A business enterprise with many computers on a network and an IT professional on duty might find this system to be perfect. But a little old lady in Miami with one computer to protect finds it unnecessarily complicated--not  impossible, but just not as simple as it should be.

I have never used one of these before and even with instructions from others I had a little trouble figuring out how to adjust it. There is also a screw underneath the mount but it doesn't need adjusting.1 - loosen the nut a couple turns2 - place the nut side on the rail first and drop the lever side down. I kept trying to do it the other way around and couldn't get it on the rail! Note: there is a pin on the mount that needs to line up with a slot on the Picatinny rail.3 - flip the lever to lock it and then tighten the screw to secure it.4 - release the lever then tighten the screw maybe 1/8 turn.5 - tighten the nut to lock the screw in place and then flip the lever to lock the mount in place.

The issues most people are seeing are due to the Blu-Ray forum's inability to define and mandate a single standard protocol for creation and display of Blu-Ray Audio/video.  The "HD" world lost out to the "Blu-ray" world (sort of like VHS and Beta or cassette and 8 track).  So from the industry standpoint, if you weren't part of the "Blu-ray" originator world, you have to play catch up every time a new release comes out.Such was the case with me.  Bought my BD570 in Mar 2011.  Got it out of the box, easy install and connection to my LAN, and it played DVDs and a couple of "older" Blu-Ray remakes fine.  When I bought Avatar (not when it first came out on BD), I had to update the LG firmware.  I did and it then played fine.  A month later, bought the BD version of Narnia, Dawn Trader.  Tried to load it.  System said I needed an update.  I downloaded the latest firmware, installed it, and it didn't work.  Talked with the LG customer support, they indicated that I wasn't on the most current version, that I should get the latest.However, was told that it probably wouldn't work, as they were having to reverse engineer the "new" way that 20th Century Fox used (providing "greater" capabilities).  They also told me that all the hardware manufacturers are faced with the same dilemma, ie a new release comes out and they have to scurry around to try and get a firmware update out so that we, the consumers, can see the "new release."Additionally, found that the latest fix "broke" my ability to see the Avatar BD.  Called back to LG, and they are sending me a disk with "an update to fix my issues".  I have had several LG products and have always been happy with them.Unfortunately, what I see is a result of industrial competition and back stabbing, all due to a lack of a standard protocol for Blu-Ray!!  Blu-ray developers and standards folks, please get your collective stuff together so that the consumers can truly enjoy a new and great technology.The only recourse I seem to have is to buy a Sony BD (Blu-ray originating from Sony), which tend to be overpriced.The issues continue.  I received the "update" for the firmware today, 5Jul11.  It still doesn't work.  I am out of warranty for return to Amazon (60 days), and LG has indicated that I only have warranty for parts.  So I a fancy DVD player!!!I am extremely disappointed with LG and Amazon customer support.

This was originally ordered for a gift but was delivered on the second day despite my payment for one-day shipping.  (To be fair to Amazon, it was ordered just minutes before "next day delivery" closed.)Despite the fact that this gift could not be given because of its late arrival - after the intended recipient (visiting family) had returned home - I was able to convince my wife that this would be an ideal birthday present for me.  I had always wanted a machine where the touch of one button gave me an excellent latte or cappuccino, which I mostly prefer to shots of espresso.Prior to buying this I had spent a considerable amount of time on the web researching other super-automatics from Jura-Capresso and many other manufacturers.  The Jura-Capresso Z5 was my preference but the features of this model appeared to be almost as good for some $600 less.  The quality of frothed milk dispensed for a cappuccino on the Z5 looked impressive on a video I checked out.I expected this model to perform similarly, but what I got was froth of very poor quality and too cold.  It had many 1/2" bubbles on the surface if I moved the froth selector closer to the "steam only" position to get warmer milk.This model will give a 16 oz coffee at the press of one button, but what you get is very weak, bitter and undrinkable.  Even a 7oz cup brewed to maximum strength was somewhat weak and bitter, since the entire 7 oz was passed through the coffee until it ran clear towards the end.  I had expected 2 or 3 (possibly 4) oz of espresso topped up automatically with hot water to the selected quantity rather than over-extraction to this extent.  The finest grind seemed rather coarse when I examined the dregs tray.  Maybe these are set up for people who like Megabucks-type charred coffee, so the oily beans don't gum up the grinder.  My preference for medium roast could certainly benefit from finer grinding.Tea or soup made with hot water from the dispenser would be a similar disappointment since the temperature of 8 oz of water hovered little more than 150 degrees (after pre-heating the cup).On the positive side, espressos of 1 or 2 oz were acceptable, though definitely not the quality of a semi-automatic machine.After some 24 hours during which I tried maybe 30 brews, changing many of the variables, I finally decided that this machine does not cut it.  My inexpensive Capresso Ultima regularly produces better cappuccinos and I prefer the "espressos" produced by my stove-top Mokka pots.Thankfully Amazon has a good return policy.  I have previously returned only one item (which had a flaw and was replaced to my complete satisfaction).  This item is currently on its way back to Amazon.  I shall treat myself to a vacuum brewer and keep looking for the perfect super automatic.
